gons_findings: Base runner filters TRAIN and calibration to base classes; initial single-model path calls fit_gons. No optional Unknown records are supplied in that fit path.
Fixed YAML inherits grid_search calibration, 512-score buffers, alpha_false_known=0.05, beta_true_support=0.9 and 64 candidate quantiles from model defaults.

Positive scores use own-class stable prototypes; impostor scores use other-class stable prototypes. Positive buffers keep the last 512 per class; the impostor buffer keeps the last 512 overall. Balanced positives then use the same count from the tail of each class buffer. Order matters.

Grid search picks the largest feasible threshold with impostor acceptance <=0.05 and positive coverage >=0.9. If none is feasible, it uses the fixed-config positive-score 0.85 quantile. Therefore 0.85 is a fallback, not the entire calibration policy.

Fixed-config NCDR refines known-class assignment separately from rejection: when the best/second-best normalized class-distance ratio exceeds0.85, it may prefer the lower-support class. Novelty score/threshold remain tied to the rejection prototype; equality is accepted.

A frozen base-session use, calibration row order, known-only calibration population, memory strategy and all effective defaults need a reviewed contract. No change to limits or parameters is authorized by this screen.
limits: Static partial source review only. No full-paper numerical equivalence, dependency environment or end-to-end candidate runtime has been verified.

opennet_batch_coverage_estimate.assumptions: Independent uniform sampling with replacement; six classes; no runtime or performance extrapolation.
opennet_batch_coverage_estimate.formula: Sum over class subsets S of (-1)^|S| * (1-sum(p_i for i in S))^128
opennet_batch_coverage_estimate.population: Existing EFC known TRAIN support, used only as a prospective tabular example

opennet_findings: Flat encoder uses slim.batch_norm without normalizer_params or is_training. Official TensorFlow1.3 defaults is_training=True and moving updates require explicit dependencies; none occur in inspected OpenNet file. Batch-dependent standalone inference is a source-based inference, not a measured runtime result.

latent and predict_prob partition input into self.batch_size chunks. Any faithful reproduction must resolve chunk composition/order and final short chunks; enabling running-stat inference would be a distinct corrected adaptation.

UnitPosNegScale assumes already-unit-scaled input and maps (x-0.5)*2. The separate unit_scale helper computes min/max anew on its input. A TRAIN-fitted tabular scaling contract is not supplied by these helpers.

Random replacement batches without every class are skipped before i increments. The iterations argument counts accepted batches, not all draws. Stratifying batches would change the reference sampling distribution.
